column3: The Hebrew has burnt offering in the singular; BSB uses plural burnt offerings.
The Hebrew leaves the appointer unnamed and uses a verb of bringing to remembrance; BSB identifies David and renders this celebrate.
The Hebrew describes giving thanks through Asaph’s hand without an explicit word song; BSB supplies this song of thanksgiving and expresses committing it to Asaph.
The Hebrew has the heart of the seekers in the singular; BSB uses plural hearts.
The Hebrew names the judgments of His mouth; BSB expresses this as judgments He has pronounced.
The Hebrew has a nominal statement that His judgments are in all the earth; BSB supplies carry throughout.
The Hebrew first addresses you in the singular and then uses your in the plural for the inheritance; BSB uses the same English pronouns for both.
The Hebrew addresses you in the plural; BSB changes to third-person they.
The Hebrew ends with from a kingdom to another people; BSB says from one kingdom to another.
The Hebrew says strength and joy are in His place; BSB supplies filling His dwelling.
The Hebrew says the splendor of holiness without a possessive expression; BSB adds His.
The Hebrew says the world will not be moved; BSB says it cannot be moved.
